notes: Loudoun Water (the retail utility for Loudoun County; Fairfax Water is only the wholesale supplier and was not used). Read off the 'Central System Water and Sewer User Rates' table, Water Usage Rates, Multifamily & Commercial line: Tier 1 $4.42 and Tier 2 $7.59 per 1,000 gallons. Took Tier 2, the top block, as the rate a very large flat-load user pays. Already published per 1,000 gallons; no unit conversion. The page prints the two commercial tiers without stating the gallon threshold between them (only the residential tiers show 0-25,000 / 25,001-50,000 / over 50,000 gal breakpoints), so the exact breakpoint could not be read off the page. Rates effective January 1, 2026. Wastewater is billed separately by Loudoun Water on the same metered volume at $6.59 per 1,000 gallons (all customers), so an all-in volumetric cost is about $14.18 per 1,000 gal. Reclaimed water on the same page is $2.07 per 1,000 gal; non-potable/irrigation is $9.34. Quarterly basic charges are additional and scale with meter size (6-inch commercial water $3,125.80/quarter).

Dallas Water Utilities, Dallas City Code Sec. 49-18.1(c)(2)(B), general (commercial) service usage charges. Three steps read off the page: up to 10,000 gal $5.32; above 10,000 gal $5.88; above 10,000 gal AND above 1.4 times the customer's own annual average monthly use $8.59. Took $5.88, the step that applies above 10,000 gal/month. Did NOT use the $8.59 step: it only triggers on seasonal peaking above 1.4x the customer's own average month, which a flat-load data center will not hit. Published per 1,000 gallons; no conversion. Effective date: the code page carries no 'eff.' note, only the amendment history ending at Ord. 33232, and the page is labeled '4/2026 Code (S-32) (current)'. Dallas resets utility rates each fiscal year on October 1, and the DWU rate insert for this schedule is titled 'City of Dallas utility fees effective October 1, 2025' (https://dallascityhall.com/departments/waterutilities/Documents/COD%20Rates%20Insert_Digital.pdf), so 2025-10 is used; that PDF itself could not be opened (robots/TLS blocked), so the effective date is inferred from its title rather than read inside it. Wastewater is billed separately under Sec. 49-18.2 on metered water volume; that section's rate is not on this page. Fort Worth is a separate utility and prices per CCF - not used.

City of Phoenix Water Services rate schedule effective March 1, 2025. 'User and Other Charges' volume rates, inside-city column: low season (Jan/Feb/Mar/Dec) $4.93 per CCF, medium season (Apr/May/Oct/Nov) $5.65, high season (Jun-Sep) $6.13. Converted at 1 CCF = 748 gal (the schedule states this): value = 5.65/0.748 = 7.55; low = 4.93/0.748 = 6.59; high = 6.13/0.748 = 8.20. Used the medium season for value because a data center runs a flat year-round load. Note the schedule does NOT publish a separate non-residential volume table - the same per-CCF volume rates apply to residential and non-residential inside the city; only the fixed monthly service charge varies by meter size and location. Outside-city volume is 150% of inside. An environmental mandate charge of $0.62 per CCF inside city (=$0.83 per 1,000 gal) is billed on top of the volume rate and is NOT included in value. Wastewater is not in this document and is billed separately.

Could not read the current rate off any City of Atlanta Department of Watershed Management page. The official 'Water and Sewer Rates' page (https://atlantawatershed.org/waterrates/) publishes only Fulton County's supplemental sewer charges (service $5.62/30 days, usage $6.72 per CCF effective 1/1/2026) plus the statement that 'Atlanta's water and sewer rates have not increased since 2012' and are held through June 30, 2028. The City's own tiers live only in the '2025 Water-Sewer Rates Fact Sheet' hosted on Google Drive (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1KdbW1uTS5iHjwtp4Vr3dYGyvy4v7DTTm/view), which is robots-disallowed and returned no text via file/view, /preview, uc?export=download and drive.usercontent download; the same file is what ATL311 KB0012935 links to as 'Get Rate Information'. The bill calculator (atlantawatershed.org/billcalculator/) loads from aws.h2o4atl.com, which fails TLS. Also checked atlanta.elaws.us Sec. 154-112 (redirect loop, unfetchable) and library.municode.com (403). So the number here comes from a live AJC news page reporting the last increase in the series: Atlanta charges three increasing tiers per CCF and a data center sits wholly in tier 3 (7+ CCF): WATER $6.16 per CCF, sewer $15.69 per CCF, effective July 1, 2011. Converted 6.16/0.748 = 8.24 per 1,000 gal. Basis is modeled, not sourced, because the figure is (a) from a news page rather than the tariff and (b) carried forward to today on the utility's 'no increase since 2012' statement, which leaves a possible 2012 step unaccounted for. Sewer is billed on the same metered water volume and is roughly 2.5x the water rate ($15.69/CCF = $20.98 per 1,000 gal), so the combined volumetric cost is far larger than the water line alone - Atlanta commonly publishes water and sewer combined, and that combined figure was deliberately NOT used here. Ignored cleanwateratlanta.h2o4atl.com: confirmed dead, now serving gambling spam.

City of Columbus Division of Water rate chart, all rates stated 'Effective January 1, 2026'. Used the INDUSTRIAL, inside-city row: $6.610 per CCF (rate codes SQIC/SMIC). Converted at 1 CCF = 748 gal: 6.610/0.748 = 8.84 per 1,000 gal. Flat per-CCF commodity charge, no volume blocks, so there is no large-user discount. Which class a data center is billed under matters here and I used INDUSTRIAL: industrial is priced ABOVE commercial in Columbus. For reference, commercial inside city is $5.850 per CCF (WMIC) = $7.82 per 1,000 gal; industrial outside city/suburban is $7.170 per CCF (SQII/SMII) = $9.59; commercial outside city $6.180 (ZQIC) = $8.26. Suburban sites such as New Albany pay the outside-city column. Residential is tiered ($4.448 first 5 CCF/mo, $4.932 over) and is not applicable. Sanitary sewer and stormwater are separate Columbus charges not included in this water figure.

City of Chicago Department of Water Management, water rate history table. Most recent effective row on the page is 6/1/2025 (+4.00%); there is no 6/1/2026 row published as of this check. Headline 'Rate' column is $36.51 per 1,000 CUBIC FEET - recording that directly would overstate cost about 7.5x. Took the adjacent 'Approximate Water Cost' column, $4.89, which the City already states per 1,000 gallons, so no conversion was needed (cross-check: 36.51/7.4805 = 4.88). Flat rate: Chicago has no customer classes and no volume blocks, so a data center pays the same volumetric rate as everyone else. Sewer is billed on the same metered water volume at 100 percent of the water charge (since 1/1/2015) as a separate line item, so the combined volumetric cost is about $9.78 per 1,000 gallons.

Salt Lake City Department of Public Utilities FY27 rates, which the page states took effect July 1, 2026. Commercial / Industrial / Institutional water: summer (April-October) $4.18 per CCF, winter (November-March) $2.58 per CCF. Converted at 1 CCF = 748 gal: summer 4.18/0.748 = 5.59 (high), winter 2.58/0.748 = 3.45 (low). value is the simple unweighted mean of the two seasonal rates ((4.18+2.58)/2 = 3.38 per CCF = 4.52 per 1,000 gal) - basis is modeled because of that averaging, not because of the unit conversion. Summer is 62% above winter, so the single annual number is misleading without the range; a real flat-load bill would be month-weighted (7 summer months / 5 winter months would give about 4.70). The obvious page slc.gov/utilities/pay-my-bill/current-rates carries residential rates only and was not used. Sewer for this class is billed on 70% of metered water consumption at $10.97 per CCF ($14.67 per 1,000 gal of sewered volume) plus $9.58/month per ERU - i.e. sewer is on the same water volume but discounted to 70% of it, and it is well above the water rate.

San Antonio Water System, General Class (commercial/industrial). SAWS splits the volumetric water charge across two separate published schedules and both must be added. (1) Water Delivery, general-class page, 'Effective for Consumption on or about January 1, 2026', inside city: base block (up to 100% of the customer's annual average monthly use) $1.958 per 1,000 gal; then $2.252 (>100-125%), $2.937 (>125-175%), $3.427 (>175%). (2) General Class Water Supply Fee, base block $3.079 per 1,000 gal (then $3.541 / $4.619 / $5.389). Sum of the base blocks = 1.958 + 3.079 = $5.037, rounded to 5.04 per 1,000 gal. Both components are already per 1,000 gallons; no unit conversion. Used the BASE block because SAWS defines blocks as a percentage of the customer's own prior-year average month, not fixed gallons - a flat-load data center sits in its own base block essentially all year and never escalates. The supply fee is larger than the delivery charge, so reading only the general-class page would understate water cost by about 61%. Basis is modeled because the two components carry different vintages: the delivery page states January 1, 2026 while the water supply fee page's table is labeled 2024 under a legacy 'effective January 1, 2023' heading, so the sum is not a single as-published number. Wastewater is billed on the same volume, flat across all usage, at $4.3680 per 1,000 gal inside city (2026), which nearly doubles the volumetric bill to about $9.41.

Portland Water Bureau, water volume charge $8.833 per CCF for the fiscal year July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (rates reset every July 1). Converted at 1 CCF = 748 gal: 8.833/0.748 = 11.81 per 1,000 gal. Flat rate - no volume blocks, no separate commercial class, so a large flat-load user pays the same volumetric rate as everyone else. Sewer (sanitary) is billed on the same metered water volume and is higher than water itself: nonresidential $14.73 per CCF = $19.69 per 1,000 gal (residential $14.24 per CCF), same FY26-27 effective period, so the combined volumetric cost is about $31.50 per 1,000 gal. Stormwater is deliberately excluded from this per-gallon rate because it is not volumetric: it is charged on impervious/developed area at $14.739 per 1,000 sq ft of billable area per 30 days.

Metropolitan Utilities District of Omaha, Rate Schedule W-3 Large Volume Industrial Water Service, effective January 2, 2026 (linked from https://www.mudomaha.com/rates-fees/). W-3 is a declining block: the first 5,000 CCF or less is a LUMP SUM of $11,456.00 (not a per-unit rate), and the marginal rate over 5,000 CCF is $1.9657 per CCF. Took the marginal over-5,000-CCF rate: 1.9657/0.748 = 2.63 per 1,000 gal (schedule states 1 CCF = 748 gal). Did not divide the lump sum by anything - at exactly 5,000 CCF it implies $2.29/CCF, and dividing it by any other volume gives a wrong number. Which schedule a data center actually qualifies for: W-3 requires an industrial process user with normal consumption of 5,000+ CCF/month and a one-year commitment, and explicitly excludes irrigation; W-4 is 'available to AND REQUIRED OF' commercial and industrial customers buying water primarily for sprinkling, lake/lagoon recharge and/or COOLING. A data center whose load is chiefly evaporative cooling would therefore be pushed onto W-4, whose over-1,100-CCF block is $2.0093 per CCF Nov-May ($2.69 per 1,000 gal) and $4.0350 per CCF Jun-Oct ($5.39 per 1,000 gal) - materially worse in summer. W-2 (general commercial/industrial) is $2.0309 per CCF Nov-May and $2.7187 Jun-Oct ($2.71 / $3.63 per 1,000 gal). Value reported is W-3 as instructed; treat W-4 as the realistic downside. A $11,456 minimum monthly commodity charge plus a meter service charge (up to $1,405/mo at 12-inch) applies under W-3, and a 2% statutory payment applies inside city/village limits. Sewer is set by the City of Omaha, not MUD, and is not included.

Des Moines Water Works, Commercial/Industrial rate table, effective January 1, 2026. Declining block: Step 1 (0-150,000 gal/mo) $7.15, Step 2 (150,001-450,000) $4.80, Step 3 (over 450,000 gal/mo) $3.70 per 1,000 gal inside the City of Des Moines. Took Step 3, the bottom marginal block, because a data center is far above 450,000 gal/month; the headline Step 1 figure is about double the true marginal rate. Already per 1,000 gallons, no conversion. Outside-city commercial/industrial is $8.85 / $6.65 / $4.75 by the same steps. Do not confuse with the residential schedule, which is increasing block, or with irrigation at $10.70 per 1,000 gal inside city. A capital improvement fee applies to some accounts on top. Sanitary sewer is a City of Des Moines charge, not a DMWW charge, and is not included here.

GAP - could not read a TMWA volumetric rate off any page. The TMWA water rates landing page lists the schedule names only ('Residential Metered Service', 'General Metered Water Service (GMWS)', 'Interruptible Service (IWS)', 'Interruptible Large Volume Nonpotable Service Rates and Charges (ILVNPS)') and shows no numbers; the rate figures sit behind click-through PDFs whose destination URLs are not exposed in the fetched page markup, so the GMWS schedule could not be opened and I will not guess a PDF path. What I tried: fetched tmwa.com/tmwa-customer-service/water-rates/ four times (asking for links, then for any dollar figures, then for the accordion contents) and tmwa.com/tmwa-customer-service/; searched for 'TMWA GMWS rate schedule pdf', 'General Metered Water Service Truckee Meadows commodity charge', site:tmwa.com rate schedule pdf, and tmwa.com/wp-content/uploads rate schedule - these returned only superseded schedule books from 2012, 2014 and 2015 (tmwa.com/docs/Customer_Services/rates/20140201_TMWA_Rate_Schedule-final.pdf and the wp-content mirror), both of which are robots-disallowed and in any case out of date; opened tmwa.com/docs/tmwa-metered-bill-explainer.pdf (explains tier 1/2/3 structure but prints no dollar amounts), tmwa.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/topics_rates_20211115.pdf (structure only, no figures), tmwa.com/financial-information/ (no ACFR link URLs exposed) and the 12/11/2025 TMWA board minutes (references a cost-of-service and rate design study, no rate table). web.archive.org is blocked by the egress proxy (403) and direct curl to tmwa.com is blocked, so I could not resolve the PDF links another way. Structural notes that stand regardless: TMWA bills NO sewer - sanitary sewer in this market is the City of Reno or Washoe County - and TMWA adds non-commodity line items (monthly service charge by meter size, and Water System Facility charges) that are easy to miss on top of any commodity rate. The Interruptible and Interruptible Large Volume Nonpotable schedules exist and are the ones worth pricing for cooling load, since nonpotable interruptible supply is normally cheaper than GMWS.

Uisce Eireann (national non-domestic tariff, applies to Dublin). Opened the Business > Billing > Charges page and read the volumetric table effective 1/10/2025-30/09/2026. Declining band structure, so per the rule I took the bottom block: Band 5 (>=2,300,000 m3/yr) water = EUR 1.39/m3. Band 4 (250,000-2,299,999 m3/yr), the band most real Dublin data centres actually fall in, is EUR 1.52/m3 -> USD 6.60/kgal, recorded as high. Band 3 (20,000-249,999) is EUR 1.71. Conversion: 1.39 / 0.87138 EUR-per-USD = USD 1.5952/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 6.04 per 1,000 US gal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/EUR 0.87138, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev (ECB daily reference rates). WASTEWATER: billed by Uisce Eireann on the same metered volume and is large - Band 4 wastewater EUR 2.40/m3 (USD 10.43/kgal), Band 3 EUR 2.45, Band 2 EUR 2.50. No wastewater rate is published for Band 5. So a Dublin site's all-in volumetric cost is roughly 2.5x the water figure alone. The page also already publishes the next year's rates (1/10/2026-30/09/2027: Band 5 water EUR 1.45, Band 4 EUR 1.47) - not used because they are not yet effective on 2026-07-31.

Waternet, business (zakelijk) drinking-water page 'Kosten met watermeter'. 2026 variabel tarief is EUR 1.18/m3 and is FLAT across all consumption bands - only the vastrecht (standing charge) steps up (0-1,000 m3 EUR 90.55/yr; 1,000-10,000 EUR 1,056; 10,000-100,000 EUR 8,561; >100,000 m3 EUR 69,368/yr). Value uses the volumetric rate only. Conversion: 1.18 / 0.87138 = USD 1.3542/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 5.13 per 1,000 US gal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/EUR 0.87138, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. BELASTING OP LEIDINGWATER (national tap-water tax): EUR 0.437/m3 in 2026, but the page states that from 2026 the ceiling above which no BOL is due moved from 300 m3 to 50,000 m3/yr - so a data centre pays BOL on its first 50,000 m3 only and its MARGINAL rate above that is the bare EUR 1.18/m3. 'high' = 1.18 + 0.437 = EUR 1.617/m3 -> USD 7.02/kgal, i.e. the effective rate inside the first 50,000 m3. 9% BTW applies on top and is recoverable by a business, so it is excluded. WASTEWATER: not billed by Waternet as a simple per-m3 volumetric charge - Amsterdam levies rioolheffing (municipal sewerage levy, banded on metered water use) and Waternet levies zuiveringsheffing per vervuilingseenheid (pollution unit), not per m3; I did not find a per-m3 equivalent on this page so no number is claimed. The provincial grondwaterheffing (groundwater levy) applies only to self-abstraction, not to metered mains supply.

Mainova AG is the retailer for Frankfurt am Main (Hessenwasser is the upstream bulk producer, not the biller). Opened the Preisblatt 'Mainova Aqua Classic' gueltig ab 01.07.2026, reached from https://www.mainova.de/de/tarife/mainova-aqua-classic. Wassermengenpreis (volumetric): EUR 2.41/m3 net, EUR 2.58/m3 gross incl. 7% MwSt. Jahresgrundpreis EUR 51.73 net / EUR 55.35 gross. The Preisblatt is a single tariff explicitly covering 'Privat- und Gewerbekunden' - Mainova publishes NO separate large-industrial block or declining tariff, so there is no top/bottom block to choose; very large sites would negotiate a Sondervertrag that is not published. Value uses the NET rate (a business recovers MwSt): 2.41 / 0.87138 = USD 2.7657/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 10.47 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' is the gross rate EUR 2.58 -> USD 11.21/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/EUR 0.87138, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. WASTEWATER: separate municipal charge from Stadtentwaesserung Frankfurt am Main, billed on the SAME metered volume - Schmutzwassergebuehr EUR 1.45/m3 (= USD 6.30 per 1,000 US gal), read at https://www.stadtentwaesserung-frankfurt.de/gebuehren-satzungen/abwassergebuehren (that page did not print an effective-from date, so the 1.45 figure is 'as published, accessed 2026-07-31'). Niederschlagswassergebuehr is EUR 0.50 per m2 of sealed area per year - area-based, not volumetric, so excluded from the per-gallon rate. All-in volumetric water+sewer is therefore about USD 16.77 per 1,000 gal.

THIS IS A WHOLESALE PRICE, NOT A RETAIL PRICE. England's non-household water market has been fully competitive since 2017, so the price a Slough data centre actually pays is a negotiated retail contract that is not published anywhere; I could not find any published retail tariff. Slough sits in Thames Water's supply area, so I used Thames Water's 'Indicative wholesale charges schedule 2026-27', effective 1 April 2026, which I opened and read. Non-household metered potable water volumetric bands: 0-20,000 m3 272.07 p/m3 (NHHMPW1-4); 20,000-50,000 m3 248.94 p/m3; 50,000-250,000 m3 204.05 p/m3; OVER 250,000 m3 163.24 p/m3 (NHHMPW7). Declining block, so value = bottom block 163.24 p/m3 = GBP 1.6324/m3. Conversion: 1.6324 / 0.74691 GBP-per-USD = USD 2.1855/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 8.27 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' = the smallest-user band 272.07 p/m3 -> USD 13.79/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/GBP 0.74691, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. Basis is 'modeled' because wholesale is being substituted for retail: a retailer adds a gross margin (typically low single-digit % of the wholesale charge) plus the retailer's own fixed fees, so true retail is somewhat above this. Large users also pay flat annual supplementary charges (intermediate GBP 4,626 / large GBP 27,071 / super-large GBP 129,096) that are not volumetric. WASTEWATER: billed on the same metered volume - non-household metered foul-drainage wholesale volumetric charge is 156.61 p/m3 for standard bands, falling to 125.28 p/m3 for users over 100,000 m3 (plus a GBP 29,756 annual supplementary charge). 125.28 p/m3 = USD 6.35 per 1,000 US gal, so sewer adds roughly 75% on top of the water rate for a large site.

Eau de Paris 'Catalogue des tarifs 2026', opened directly; tariffs effective 1 January 2026. Eau de Paris publishes ONE volumetric tariff - there is no separate tarif non-domestique and no volume blocks, so a large industrial user pays the same per-m3 as everyone else (only the part fixe / abonnement varies with meter size). Value = the all-in WATER-side volumetric total, summing the components printed in the catalogue (all EUR/m3 TTC): fourniture d'eau potable 1.1942 + redevance soutien d'etiage 0.0074 + redevance prelevement sur la ressource en eau 0.0928 + redevance Voies Navigables de France 0.0169 + redevance performance reseaux d'eau potable 0.0406 + redevance consommation d'eau (Agence de l'eau Seine-Normandie) 0.3587 = EUR 1.7106/m3. Conversion: 1.7106 / 0.87138 = USD 1.9633/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 7.43 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' = the bare fourniture d'eau potable 1.1942 -> USD 5.19/kgal. 'high' = the complete bill including assainissement -> EUR 4.2142/m3 -> USD 18.31/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/EUR 0.87138, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. Basis 'modeled' because the value is a sum of six separately-printed line items, not a single figure read off the page. WASTEWATER: billed on exactly the same metered volume and it is the larger half of the bill - collecte des eaux usees (Ville de Paris / SAP) EUR 0.6699/m3, transport et epuration (SIAAP) EUR 1.6984/m3, redevance performance reseaux de collecte EUR 0.1353/m3, total EUR 2.5036/m3 = USD 10.88 per 1,000 US gal. Figures are TTC (5.5% VAT on water supply, 10% on assainissement); a business recovers VAT, so net-of-VAT costs are ~5% lower. Cross-check: Eau de Paris's own price page (https://www.eaudeparis.fr/prix-de-leau) quotes EUR 4.23 TTC/m3 all-in for 2026, consistent with the EUR 4.2142 sum above.

Lulea kommun 'VA-taxa 2026 - Taxa foer Lulea kommuns allmaenna vatten- och avloppsanlaeggning', opened directly; taxan traeder i kraft 2026-01-01. Brukningsavgift, rorlig avgift: VATTEN 21.25 SEK/m3 excl. moms (26.56 SEK/m3 incl. 25% moms). There is no declining or increasing block - the rorliga avgift is flat. The taxa does carry separate tariff codes for hyres- och industrifastighet (VA2,5HI / V2,5HI / A2,5HI), but those differ only in the fixed annual charge; the per-m3 rate is identical, so an industrial site pays the same volumetric rate. Value uses the ex-moms rate (a business recovers moms): 21.25 / 9.5938 SEK-per-USD = USD 2.2150/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 8.38 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' is the incl-moms rate 26.56 SEK/m3 -> USD 10.48/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/SEK 9.5938, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. WASTEWATER: billed on the same metered volume at exactly the same rate - avlopp/spillvatten 21.25 SEK/m3 ex moms (USD 8.38 per 1,000 US gal), so combined VA is 42.50 SEK/m3 ex moms = USD 16.77 per 1,000 US gal. A site of hyperscale size would in practice negotiate a separate industrial agreement outside this published taxa (as the northern Swedish DC market generally does), so treat the published taxa as an upper bound on the volumetric rate.

Oslo kommune, Vann- og avloepsetaten, page 'Vann- og avloepsgebyrer'. Read the table 'Priser for beregning av vann- og avloepsgebyrer fra 1. januar 2026'. VANN: 43.23 kr/m3 ekskl. mva (49.71 kr/m3 inkl. 15% mva). Oslo charges a single flat kr/m3 - there are no consumption blocks and no separate naerings/industri tariff, so a large flat-load customer pays the same volumetric rate as everyone else; only the fixed abonnementsgebyr scales. Value uses the ex-mva rate (a business recovers mva): 43.23 / 9.5641 NOK-per-USD = USD 4.5198/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 17.11 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' is the inkl-mva rate 49.71 kr/m3 -> USD 19.67/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/NOK 9.5641, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. WASTEWATER: billed on the same metered water volume - avloep 28.81 kr/m3 ekskl. mva (33.13 kr/m3 inkl. mva) = USD 11.40 per 1,000 US gal ex mva. Combined vann + avloep = 72.04 kr/m3 ex mva = USD 28.51 per 1,000 US gal, i.e. sewer adds about two-thirds on top of the water rate. Oslo is by a wide margin the most expensive potable water in this 13-market set.

PUB non-domestic potable water. The current PUB water-price page (https://www.pub.gov.sg/Public/WaterLoop/Water-Price) publishes its tables as images that cannot be read as text, so I used PUB's own press release with the annex price tables, which I opened and read. NON-DOMESTIC potable water, S$/m3, from 1 April 2025: Water Tariff 1.43 + Water Conservation Tax 0.72 + Waterborne Fee 1.09 = TOTAL 3.24 (all figures before GST; the total is printed in the table, not derived by me). Singapore's non-domestic tariff is flat - there are no consumption blocks. I found no evidence of a further revision taking effect in 2026, so the 1 April 2025 rates are current. Conversion: 3.24 / 1.2875 SGD-per-USD = USD 2.5165/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 9.53 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' = tariff + WCT only (S$2.15, i.e. excluding the waterborne/used-water element) -> USD 6.32/kgal. 'high' = S$3.24 grossed up for 9% GST (S$3.5316) -> USD 10.38/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/SGD 1.2875, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. WASTEWATER: the Waterborne Fee IS the used-water charge and is levied on the same metered volume - S$1.09/m3 = USD 3.21 per 1,000 US gal, already included in the 3.24 total above per the row instruction. NEWATER (reclaimed - what a Singapore data centre would actually buy for cooling): from 1 April 2025, Tariff 1.28 + WCT 0.13 + Waterborne 1.09 = TOTAL S$2.50/m3 before GST = USD 7.35 per 1,000 US gal, about 23% cheaper than potable. Same source table. PUB also lists an Industrial Water tariff but no figures for it appear in this press release.

Tokyo Metropolitan Government Bureau of Waterworks. The Bureau's own rate pages (waterworks.metro.tokyo.lg.jp) return HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so I read the statutory tariff table in the Tokyo Metropolitan Water Supply Ordinance (Toukyou-to kyuusui jourei) on the TMG regulations site, which I opened successfully. Steeply INCREASING block tariff, so per the rule I took the TOP block. Juuryou ryoukin (volumetric), yen/m3: 5-10 m3 22; 10-20 m3 128; 20-30 m3 163; 30-50 m3 202; 50-100 m3 213; 100-200 m3 298; 200-1,000 m3 372; OVER 1,000 m3 404. A data centre is unambiguously in the over-1,000 m3 top block. Kihon ryoukin (fixed monthly charge) scales with meter diameter for a large-diameter service: 100mm JPY 94,568; 150mm JPY 159,094; 200mm JPY 349,434; 250mm JPY 480,135; 300mm and above JPY 816,145 per month - fixed, not volumetric, so excluded from the per-gallon rate. The ordinance states the tabulated amounts are the base multiplied by 110/100, i.e. they INCLUDE 10% consumption tax. Value uses the published tax-inclusive JPY 404/m3: 404 / 162.94 JPY-per-USD = USD 2.4794/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 9.39 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' is the tax-exclusive equivalent (404/1.1 = JPY 367.27/m3), which is what a business effectively bears after recovering consumption tax -> USD 8.53/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/JPY 162.94, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. LAST_VERIFIED CAVEAT: the ordinance text I read does not print an effective-from date alongside the table; the tax-inclusive figures reflect the 10% consumption tax rate in force since October 2019, so I recorded 2019-10 as the earliest date these exact yen figures can date from. SEWERAGE: billed separately by the TMG Bureau of Sewerage on the same metered volume and is also steeply increasing - top block (over 1,000 m3) JPY 345/m3, read at https://donichi-suidou.com/tokyo-suidou-ryoukin/ (a secondary source, used because the Bureau's own pages 403) = USD 8.02 per 1,000 US gal, so sewer adds roughly 85% on top of the water rate.

SABESP, regulated by ARSESP. SABESP's own site (sabesp.com.br) blocks automated fetches, so I used ARSESP's signed technical note 'NT 1o Reajuste Tarifario da SABESP - Tarifa de Aplicacao - URAE-1', which I opened and read; the new tarifas de aplicacao take effect 1 January 2026 (reajuste of 6.1106% plus 0.3558% for tax updates). Tabela 1, category COMERCIAL / INDUSTRIAL / PUBLICA (sem contrato), quoted verbatim from the document: 0-10 m3 R$ 81.57/month fixed; 11-20 m3 R$ 15.95/m3; 21-50 m3 R$ 30.57/m3; ACIMA DE 50 m3 R$ 31.84/m3 - identical figures for Tarifa Agua and Tarifa Esgoto. This is an increasing block tariff, so per the rule value = the top block, R$ 31.84/m3 water. Conversion: 31.84 / 5.1006 BRL-per-USD = USD 6.2424/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 23.63 per 1,000 US gal. 'low' = the 21-50 m3 block (R$ 30.57) -> USD 22.69/kgal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/BRL 5.1006, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. Basis is 'modeled' because the document contains ten regional tables and does not name Sao Paulo capital explicitly; I identified Tabela 1 as the capital's table because it covers SABESP's metropolitan business units OC, OL, OO, ON and OS (Centro, Leste, Oeste, Norte, Sul - the city of Sao Paulo) and because it carries the highest tariffs in the document, matching the metropolitan region. Cross-checked against the pre-privatisation base table (Deliberacao ARSESP 1.514/2024, reproduced in Anexo IV at https://semil.sp.gov.br/desestatizacaosabesp/wp-content/uploads/sites/24/2024/05/Anexo-IV.pdf), where the same category shows R$ 29.90-equivalent levels that escalate to R$ 31.84 under the 1.061106 x 1.003558 adjustment. WASTEWATER - CONFIRMED: SABESP charges esgoto at EXACTLY THE SAME rate as agua in every band (R$ 31.84/m3 in the top block), on the same metered volume. The true all-in volumetric cost of a Sao Paulo site is therefore R$ 63.68/m3 = USD 47.26 per 1,000 US gal, precisely double the headline water figure. Note also that the table is the 'sem contrato' schedule; a very large industrial customer can sign a demanda-firme contract with SABESP at negotiated rates that are not published.

City of Toronto, Toronto Water. Read the water-rate table on the City's 'Water Rates & Fees' page, effective 1 January 2026. Two-block declining structure: BLOCK 1 (up to 5,000 m3/yr) CAD 4.8629/m3 on-time (CAD 5.1188 late); BLOCK 2 (consumption over 5,000 m3/yr) CAD 3.3219/m3 on-time (CAD 3.4967 late). THE INDUSTRIAL WATER RATE PROGRAM STILL EXISTS and Block 2 is exactly that programme - the page states 'Block 2 rates apply to businesses participating in the Industrial Water Rate Program', and Council approved a 3.75% increase for Block 1 versus only 1.25% for Block 2 for 2026. A data centre enrolled in the programme therefore pays the Block 2 rate, which is 32% below Block 1; if it is NOT enrolled it pays Block 1 on everything, which is why Block 1 is recorded as 'high'. Value = CAD 3.3219/m3 (on-time payment; late payment adds 5.26%). Conversion: 3.3219 / 1.4046 CAD-per-USD = USD 2.3650/m3; / 0.264172 = USD 8.95 per 1,000 US gal. 'high' = Block 1 CAD 4.8629/m3 -> USD 13.11 per 1,000 US gal. FX: ECB reference rate USD/CAD 1.4046, pulled 2026-07-30 from api.frankfurter.dev. WASTEWATER: no separate volumetric sewer rate appears on this page - the only 'Wastewater Fees' listed are one-off service-connection and technical-review charges (CAD 440.78 to CAD 14,718.78), not a per-m3 charge. The Block 1 / Block 2 consumption rates are the consumption charge shown on the Toronto utility bill; I did not find a second per-m3 sewer line item to add, so no sewer number is claimed here. Toronto also bills a separate stormwater/solid-waste line that is not volumetric.

SAWS Recycled Water Service rate page, rates effective January 1, 2026. Observed $/acre: Elmendorf 44ac $16,000; Floresville 83ac $26,687; Von Ormy 133ac $37,594; Atascosa 15.3ac $45,751; San Antonio 78263 27.6ac $52,536; Schertz 133ac $52,632; San Antonio 78266 20.9ac $62,201; Converse 49ac $71,429; Elmendorf 54.4ac $99,926; Elmendorf 10.9ac $326,493. Low and high are min and max. Value=$99,926 (Elmendorf 54.4-acre site) = upper end of the clustered range; the $326,493 figure is a single 10.9-acre lot priced far above every other parcel in the set and is held as high only, per the method's warning that small lots price per acre far higher. Asking prices, hence modeled.

WEAK ROW - read the caveat. No 10+ acre INDUSTRIAL-tagged listing exists anywhere in the Portland metro on either aggregator: LandSearch Portland radius returns 0, and the Oregon statewide industrial 10+ acre query returns 17 listings, all in central/coastal/southern Oregon (Prineville, Roseburg, Newport, Coos Bay, Independence, Hines) with none in Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas or Columbia counties. Low=$25,363, value and high=$58,911 (upper end). CAUTION: these are large rural-fringe parcels (one is a leased rock-products site, the Cornelius ones are nursery ground) and materially understate serviced industrial land inside the UGB - on the same source, sub-10-acre commercial parcels in the metro ask $356,812/ac (Sandy), $433,428/ac (Forest Grove), $482,233/ac (Estacada infill) and $648,701/ac (Canby). If this row is used for a serviced site, the sub-10-acre band is the better guide.

Aggregate of live listings (source type c). The industrial-tagged 10+ acre query for Nebraska returns 9 listings and NONE are in the Omaha metro (Douglas, Sarpy, Cass, Washington, Saunders) - they are North Platte, Seward, Fremont, Auburn, Crete. Low=$89,286, high=$431,970. Aggregate of live listings (source type c). LandSearch Des Moines radius, tag=industrial, size min 10 acres: 4 listings, 3 with published prices - Indianola 30.2ac $62,854/acre; Indianola 27.1ac $70,055/acre; Ankeny 10ac $95,000/acre. Aggregate of live listings (source type c). LandSearch Nevada statewide, tag=industrial, size min 10 acres = 53 listings; filtered by hand to the northern Nevada / Reno-Sparks-Fernley industrial corridor (Washoe, Storey, Lyon, Carson) = 4 usable: Yerington 18ac $6,806; Silver Springs 39ac $7,667; Fernley 181ac $21,853; Dayton 131ac $45,802. Dublin, large employment/industrial-zoned parcels. Two comparables, both well over 10 acres. (1) Lisney GDA Development Land Q1 2025 report, printed on the page: Dublin Central Logistics Park, Finglas, 'approximately 91.4 acres... sold in three lots for a total of EUR 27.6m' = EUR 301,969/acre (transaction, Q1 2025) - this is the value. (2) Irish Times, Killamonan Business Park, Dublin 15, 47.92 ha (118.40 acres) zoned entirely general employment under the Fingal County Development Plan, guiding EUR 35m = EUR 295,608/acre (asking, Feb 2022) - this is the low. Freehold. FX: 1 EUR = 1.147605 USD (USD/EUR 0.87138), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. EUR 301,969/acre x 1.147605 = USD 346,541/acre. Basis modeled because the per-acre rate is derived by dividing a lot-total by acreage, not printed as a per-acre figure. Caveat: these are general industrial/logistics land rates; purpose-built data-centre land at Grange Castle/Profile Park trades higher, but I could not open a live source confirming that (estatesgazette.co.uk article headlined 'Dublin industrial land hits record price of EUR 1m per acre' returned HTTP 403, property.ie and search.savills.com listing pages returned redirect loops / 403, so no third live listing was obtainable).

PROXY, not Amsterdam city. Gemeente Hollands Kroon Grondprijzenbrief 2025 (in force 1 Jan 2025 - 19 Mar 2026), printed prices for municipal bedrijventerreinen: Robbenplaat II EUR 115.00/m2 and Industrieweg EUR 115.00/m2, with a general bedrijventerrein table figure of EUR 100.00/m2. Value = upper end EUR 115/m2; low = EUR 100/m2. EUR 115/m2 x 4046.86 m2/acre = EUR 465,389/acre; x 1.147605 = USD 534,083/acre. FX: 1 EUR = 1.147605 USD (USD/EUR 0.87138), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold (uitgifte in eigendom). Why this proxy: Hollands Kroon (Middenmeer / Agriport A7) is where the Amsterdam region's hyperscale data centres are actually built; Amsterdam city itself issues land only in erfpacht (leasehold) and its Grondprijzenbeleid (opened at lokaleregelgeving.overheid.nl/CVDR672018/2 and zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/gmb-2022-32578.html) publishes only office/residential EUR/m2 bvo, no bedrijventerrein land price; Haarlemmermeer states in its Programmabegroting (programmabegroting.haarlemmermeer.nl/2026 and /2023, paragraaf grondbeleid) that its Grondprijzennota is 'geheim van aard' and publishes no figures. Also opened, all wrong municipality or no figure: CVDR752764 and CVDR731454 (Brunssum), CVDR735485 (Epe), CVDR735345 (Lansingerland), exb-2025-3387 (Goeree-Overflakkee, EUR 143-149/m2). Treat this row as an out-of-metro floor: serviced industrial land inside the Amsterdam ring is materially more expensive than EUR 115/m2.

BORIS-Portal, Bodenrichtwerte for gewerbliche Bauflaechen (commercial/industrial building land) in Frankfurt am Main, Stichtag 01.01.2024. Printed on the page: Minimalwert 250 EUR/m2, Maximalwert 850 EUR/m2 (down 10.5% from 950), Durchschnitt 369 EUR/m2. low = 250 EUR/m2 = USD 1,161,049/acre; high = 850 EUR/m2 = USD 3,947,567/acre. Value = the citywide average 369 EUR/m2 = 369 x 4046.86 = EUR 1,493,291/acre x 1.147605 = USD 1,713,709/acre, because the 850 EUR/m2 maximum is a small prime inner-city commercial plot that a parcel over 10 acres could not be assembled at - 369 is the upper end of what is plausible for a large GE/GI industrial site. FX: 1 EUR = 1.147605 USD (USD/EUR 0.87138), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Caveat: 'gewerbliche Bauflaechen' mixes commercial with industrial; a pure Industrie (GI) breakout was not obtainable - frankfurt.de's Immobilienmarktbericht 2026 PDF returned HTTP 403, and aktuelle-grundstueckspreise.de publishes Bauland (residential) only for Frankfurt.

Knight Frank Industrial Land Values Research 2022. Slough is named and priced on the page: average industrial land value GBP 3.46m per acre, Q1 2022 (up GBP 1.76m / 103% since Q1 2019), and Slough is the highest of all South East local authorities listed. Value = GBP 3,460,000/acre x 1.338849 = USD 4,632,419/acre. low = GBP 2.51m/acre (Welwyn Hatfield, the lowest South East authority in the same table) = USD 3,360,512; high = Slough's own GBP 3.46m. Other SE points on the page for context: Spelthorne GBP 3.42m, Runnymede GBP 3.41m, Thurrock GBP 3.03m, South Buckinghamshire GBP 2.64m. Values are modelled by Knight Frank on a standardised 20,000 sq m warehouse, i.e. large-parcel basis. Freehold. FX: 1 GBP = 1.338849 USD (USD/GBP 0.74691), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. On the MHCLG/DLUHC route: I found the current dataset (gov.uk/government/publications/land-value-estimates-for-policy-appraisal-2023, valuation date 1 Oct 2023) but the per-authority industrial figures live only in the .xlsx/.ods attachments, which are binary and could not be opened by any available fetch tool; the HTML 'guidelines for use' page confirms 119 industrial valuations were done but prints no local-authority table, and the 2015 PDF prints only an England mean (GBP 482,000/ha). Cross-check on order of magnitude: Colliers (colliers.com/en-gb/news/25-03-22-industrial-land-values-are-reaching-record-levels-in-london-and-south-east) puts South East industrial land at GBP 2.5m/acre and London at GBP 7.1m/acre on Jan 2022 data. Both sources are 2022 - UK industrial land has moved since, so this is a floor, not a current quote.

Arthur Loyd Ile-de-France land-for-sale listings (live, current asking prices), industrial/artisanal-use terrains. Parcels of 1 ha or more on that page: 39,269 m2 at EUR 734,853 = EUR 18.71/m2 (Seine-et-Marne); 19,871 m2 at EUR 1,390,970 = EUR 70.00/m2 (Seine-et-Marne); 14,677 m2 at EUR 1,050,000 = EUR 71.54/m2 (Villiers-en-Biere); 13,443 m2 at EUR 2,000,000 = EUR 148.78/m2 (Montereau-Fault-Yonne). Value = upper end EUR 148.78/m2 x 4046.86 = EUR 602,090/acre x 1.147605 = USD 690,964/acre. low = EUR 18.71/m2 = USD 86,907/acre. Smaller inner-ring plots on the same page run higher (Lisses 5,000 m2 at EUR 300/m2, Saint-Soupplets 5,704 m2 at EUR 280/m2), which a 10-acre-plus site would not reach. Cross-check: solumat.fr (dated 3 Jun 2026) prints a France-wide industrial land average of EUR 120/m2 in 2026 with a range of EUR 15-150/m2, consistent with the Ile-de-France upper end used here. FX: 1 EUR = 1.147605 USD (USD/EUR 0.87138), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Basis modeled: asking prices from listings, per-m2 rates derived by me from price divided by surface. Only one listing exceeded 10 acres (the 39,269 m2 / 9.7-acre Seine-et-Marne parcel), so the large-parcel sample is thin; bureauxlocaux.com had a single 62,000 m2 industrial parcel in Ile-de-France (Ribecourt-Dreslincourt) but priced 'nous consulter'.

Lulea kommun municipal industrial land prices. Value from Hertsofaltet, the large-parcel green-industry field where a data centre would actually go: Norrbottens-Kuriren (published 12 Jan 2023) reports the municipality raising the price from SEK 140/m2 to SEK 300/m2, after an external valuer put the land at SEK 250-350/m2. Value = SEK 300/m2 x 4046.86 = SEK 1,214,058/acre x 0.104234 = USD 126,546/acre. low = SEK 250/m2 (bottom of the independent valuation) = USD 105,455/acre. high = SEK 450/m2 = USD 189,819/acre, which is the municipality's published price for the two Storheden verksamhetstomter offered Nov 2025 (Vart Lulea, 19 Nov 2025) - but those plots are only ~2,500 m2 and ~2,600 m2, so that rate is a small-plot price and would not apply to a parcel over 10 acres. FX: 1 SEK = 0.104234 USD (USD/SEK 9.5938), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold sale by the municipality, connection fees (anslutningsavgifter) charged on top per lulea.se/samhalle--utveckling/mark-och-exploatering/mark-for-verksamheter.html, which itself publishes no price. Value figure is from 2023 and is likely low today given Storheden reached SEK 450/m2 by late 2025.

NOT FOUND - no live source prints an industrial/logistics land price for the Oslo region. Searched: Oslo industritomt/naeringstomt price per square metre 2025, tomt til salgs industri logistikk. Opened and rejected: finn.no/realestate/plots/search.html?location=0.20061 (all 31 Oslo plots are residential building plots, 396-8,642 m2, no industrial land); finn.no/realestate/businesssale/search.html?location=0.20061 (52 commercial results, one undeveloped plot and it is residential development, Munkerudkleiva 1,550 m2 at NOK 35m); metra.no/til-salgs (nine naeringstomt listings but all outside the Oslo region - Gressvik, Nesodden, Saltnes, Vaaler, Slitu, Rakkestad, Skiptvet - and none shows a price); oslologistikkparkgardermoen.no and /omrade/ (the right product, 1.4 million m2 regulated and building-ready at Gardermoen, plots of 38.4-270.3 ha, but no price published - contact-only); meglertipset.no/artikler/selge-bolig/selge-tomt (dated 16 Jan 2026, prints NOK 5,000-15,000/m2 for central Oslo and NOK 200-1,000/m2 for outlying municipalities, but this is generic/residential land, not industrial, and not tied to a submarket - deriving a per-acre industrial figure from it would be a guess). finn.no/realestate/businessplot/search.html returned 404. Web search quota was exhausted before a Norwegian municipal naeringstomt price list (e.g. Ullensaker/Gardermoen) could be located. Left blank rather than guessed.

LEASEHOLD, NOT FREEHOLD - the key comparability caveat for Singapore. All industrial land here is state land sold on a fixed lease term; there is no freehold industrial land, so a per-acre figure is not like-for-like with the freehold markets in the other rows. Source: JTC 'Historical data on IGLS sites sold by JTC' (Industrial Government Land Sales), file dated 26 Jun 2026. Value = Plot B Tukang Innovation Drive, awarded 8 Oct 2025, site area 18,722.2 m2, 33-year lease, successful tender SGD 95,188,888 = SGD 5,084.28 per m2 of SITE area (the file's own price column is per m2 per plot ratio at PR 2.5, i.e. SGD 2,033.71 - I divided total price by land area to get a land rate). SGD 5,084.28/m2 x 4046.86 = SGD 20,575,414/acre x 0.776699 = USD 15,980,178/acre. low = Plot A Tuas Bay Drive, awarded 14 Nov 2025, 6,338.1 m2, 23-year lease, SGD 4,885,000 = SGD 770.74/m2 = USD 2,422,584/acre. Other western-industrial comparables from the same file: Penjuru Road 23 Jan 2026, 20,852.9 m2, 33 yr, SGD 87,400,890 = SGD 4,191.31/m2; Pioneer Road 28 Aug 2025, 28,058.4 m2, 33 yr, SGD 88,190,020 = SGD 3,143.09/m2; Gul Drive 20 Jun 2025, 4,876.3 m2, 23 yr = SGD 984.51/m2. FX: 1 SGD = 0.776699 USD (USD/SGD 1.2875), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. PARCEL SIZE CAVEAT: Singapore does not release industrial parcels over 10 acres - the largest recent IGLS site is 28,058 m2 (6.93 acres), so no listing meets the over-10-acre filter. Separately, JTC's posted land RENT (not price) for 2H2026 effective 1 Jul 2026 runs SGD 13.41/m2/yr (Tuas View, PR up to 1.0) to SGD 90.66/m2/yr (Telok Blangah, PR up to 3.0), escalating up to 5.5%/yr - see jtc.gov.sg/-/media/project/jtc-cx/corpweb/assets/find-land/land-rates/cx-land-rents-2h2026-with-impt-notes_.pdf. Basis modeled: per-acre land rate derived by me from tender total divided by site area.

SUBMARKET: Inzai City, Chiba (Chiba New Town) - the outer industrial belt where Tokyo's data centres are actually built, not central Tokyo. Source: 2026 koji chika (公示地価, MLIT published land price, valuation date 1 Jan 2026), industrial-zone (工業地) survey points in Inzai-shi. Two industrial points exist and both are printed: Kashiguro-minami 1-chome 3-ban (鹿黒南1丁目3番), a warehouse/logistics site 2,900 m from Chiba Newtown Chuo station, at JPY 85,700/m2, +13.51% year on year (tochidai.info); and Matsuzakidai (松崎台) at JPY 58,000/m2, +11.6% (totinokati.com, which rounds the Kashiguro point to 8.6 man yen/m2). Value = upper point JPY 85,700/m2 x 4046.86 = JPY 346,815,902/acre x 0.006137 = USD 2,128,488/acre. low = JPY 58,000/m2 = USD 1,440,517/acre. For reference, JPY 85,700/m2 = JPY 283,305/tsubo (1 tsubo = 3.30579 m2). FX: 1 JPY = 0.006137 USD (USD/JPY 162.94), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Basis modeled: koji chika is a per-m2 assessed standard value for a notional standard site, not a transacted price for an over-10-acre parcel, and the per-acre conversion is mine; also only two industrial survey points exist in the municipality, so the range is thin. The Chiba prefecture koji chika page (pref.chiba.lg.jp/youchi/toukeidata/chika/) returned HTTP 403, so the figures were read off these two Japanese land-price aggregators, which republish the MLIT data point-by-point.

SUBMARKET: Taloja / Navi Mumbai - Panvel MIDC belt, the outer industrial area where Mumbai's data centres are built, not the island city. Source: MIDC (Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation) land rate schedule, 'MIDC Land Rates, Updated 2026', Group Scheme A. Printed rates: Taloja INR 12,100/m2; Taloja Zone-II INR 15,460/m2; Additional Taloja INR 15,460/m2 (all industrial). Value = upper end INR 15,460/m2 x 4046.86 = INR 62,564,455/acre x 0.01045 = USD 653,824/acre. low = INR 12,100/m2 = USD 511,725/acre. Context on the same page: Patalganga INR 4,840/m2, Roha INR 1,260/m2 (far outer), Marol MMR Zone-I INR 63,180/m2 (city, not comparable). TENURE: MIDC does not sell freehold - plots are allotted on a 95-year lease and the quoted rate is the one-time lease premium, plus annual ground rent and transfer charges. FX: 1 INR = 0.01045 USD (USD/INR 95.69), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Basis modeled: mahaindustry.com is a third-party republication of the MIDC schedule rather than the MIDC circular itself, and the per-acre figure is my conversion. Open-market resale of MIDC plots in Taloja typically clears above the MIDC allotment rate; ilovenavimumbai.com/navi-mumbai-industrial-land-values-rents-and-yield-guide/ confirms the INR 12,100/m2 Taloja benchmark and an INR 31,390/m2 TTC-belt benchmark but prints no date, so it was not used for the value.

SUBMARKET: Barueri / Alphaville Industrial / Tambore, the Sao Paulo data-centre cluster on the Rodovia Castelo Branco axis, not the city centre. Source: Lopes live land-for-sale listings in Alphaville Industrial, Barueri. Largest parcels printed on the page: 291,874 m2 (29.2 ha) at BRL 111,000,000 on Rodovia Presidente Castelo Branco = BRL 380.30/m2; 47,000 m2 (4.7 ha) at BRL 25,000,000 in Aldeia da Serra = BRL 531.91/m2; 34,422 m2 (3.44 ha) at BRL 36,000,000 on Avenida Grimaldo Tolaini = BRL 1,045.84/m2. Value = upper end BRL 1,045.84/m2 x 4046.86 = BRL 4,232,196/acre x 0.196055 = USD 829,786/acre. low = BRL 380.30/m2 = USD 301,733/acre (and this is the only listing comfortably over 10 acres, so it is the most method-compliant single data point - the value sits at the top of the observed band, per instruction). FX: 1 BRL = 0.196055 USD (USD/BRL 5.1006), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Basis modeled: asking prices, per-m2 rates derived by me. Excluded as not comparable: a 5,687 m2 Barueri industrial listing at BRL 11,000/m2 (paulobio.com.br/terreno-industrial-sao-paulo__13437) - that is small-lot Alphaville pricing, ~20x the large-parcel rate. Hortolandia listing portals (trovit) returned HTTP 401 and nestoria/sannini returned 401 / robots-disallowed, so the Campinas-Hortolandia leg of the SP data-centre market is not represented here; Barueri only.

Vivanuncios live industrial land listings, Queretaro state. Printed listings and the per-m2 rates I derived: Felipe Carrillo Puerto 12,030 m2 at MXN 45,714,000 = MXN 3,800.00/m2; Libramiento Norponiente, Huertas La Joya 10,046 m2 at MXN 37,675,000 = MXN 3,750.25/m2; Felipe Carrillo Puerto 17,157 m2 at MXN 62,625,000 = MXN 3,650.11/m2; Granja Cedros 17,500 m2 at MXN 52,500,000 = MXN 3,000.00/m2. Value = upper end MXN 3,800/m2 x 4046.86 = MXN 15,378,068/acre x 0.057471 = USD 883,792/acre. low = MXN 3,000/m2 = USD 697,730/acre. FX: 1 MXN = 0.057471 USD (USD/MXN 17.4001), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. TWO REAL CAVEATS, both against the value being too high: (1) every one of these parcels is between 1 and 1.8 ha, i.e. none meets the over-10-acre filter, and small parcels carry a size premium - a 10-acre-plus tract in a Queretaro industrial park would clear well below MXN 3,800/m2; (2) the single listing on the page that does exceed 10 acres, Carretera 500 in El Marques at 1,231,266 m2 (123 ha) for MXN 73,000,000, implies MXN 59.3/m2 (~USD 13,800/acre), which is implausible for serviced industrial-park land and reads as a listing error, so I did not use it as the low. Tetakawi's Queretaro site-selection piece (insights.tetakawi.com/industrial-real-estate-in-queretaro-site-selection) quotes only lease rates (USD 4.00-4.10/m2/month) and is dated Dec 2020, so it was not used. Treat this row as an upper bound with a wide downside.

CBRE GTA Industrial Market Report, GTA West submarket (Mississauga / Brampton / Milton / Caledon / Halton - where GTA industrial and data-centre development actually happens). Average industrial land price printed per acre: CAD 1,779,259/acre in Q3 2025 and CAD 1,761,466/acre in Q4 2025. Value = upper end CAD 1,779,259 x 0.711946 = USD 1,266,737/acre; low = CAD 1,761,466 = USD 1,254,069/acre. FX: 1 CAD = 0.711946 USD (USD/CAD 1.4046), ECB reference rate via Frankfurter API, pulled 2026-07-30. Freehold. Basis modeled: CBRE publishes a submarket AVERAGE land price, not a parcel-level transaction, and it is not filtered to parcels over 10 acres. Development charges are a large additional per-sq-ft cost on top of land and vary sharply by municipality (Q4 2025, per the same report: Vaughan CAD 59.97/sq ft, Mississauga CAD 35.55, Brampton CAD 34.52, Milton CAD 32.26, Etobicoke CAD 1.57) - worth carrying separately in the model. Avison Young's GTA Q2 2025 report returned HTTP 403 so no second brokerage cross-check was obtainable.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), 'Data centre cost index 2025 - index scores and US$ per watt' market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'North Virginia' = US$10.92/W. Conversion: 10.92 USD/W x 1000 = 10920 USD per kW of IT load. T&T methodology page states the benchmark basis is a typical air-cooled build-to-suit hyperscale data centre of 30-50MW IT load, same basis as the pre-filled Singapore (14.53/W) and Tokyo (15.15/W) rows.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'Dallas' = US$9.54/W. Conversion: 9.54 x 1000 = 9540 USD per kW of IT load. Dallas is T&T's only Texas market and is used here for the DFW metro.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'Phoenix' = US$9.823/W. Conversion: 9.823 x 1000 = 9823 USD per kW of IT load.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'Atlanta' = US$9.9045/W. Conversion: 9.9045 x 1000 = 9904.5, rounded to 9905 USD per kW of IT load.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Columbus IS covered by T&T (contrary to the initial assumption in the task brief). Market row 'Columbus' = US$9.79/W. Conversion: 9.79 x 1000 = 9790 USD per kW of IT load.

Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition), market chart on the Data centre cost trends page. Market row 'Chicago' = US$11.232/W. Conversion: 11.232 x 1000 = 11232 USD per kW of IT load.

Salt Lake City is NOT a market in the Turner & Townsend Data Centre Construction Cost Index 2025-2026 (9th edition; 52 markets covered). Virginia / Loudoun. INSTRUMENT: retail SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on data center equipment (Va. Code Sec. 58.1-609.3(18)), not a property tax abatement. The exemption is not a fixed number of years: VEDP states it runs 'from the date of the data center's MOU through June 30, 2035', so the term is the remaining life of the program at the date the qualifying MOU is signed. An MOU executed in 2026 therefore yields ~9 years (value = 2035 sunset minus 2026), which is why basis is modeled rather than sourced. Thresholds (150M USD capex / 50 jobs at 150% of local average wage; 70M USD / 10 jobs in distressed localities from 1 Jul 2023) must generally be met within 3 years of the MOU. High end of 24 years = MOUs signed on or after 1 Jan 2023 that commit 100B USD capex and 2,500 jobs, which extend the exemption to 2050 (35B USD / 1,000 jobs extends to 2040). Cross-checked against the Virginia Dept of Taxation report to the General Assembly dated 2 Jan 2026 (https://rga.lis.virginia.gov/Published/2026/RD40/PDF), which reports 56 companies claiming the exemption in FY2025 but does not state a per-facility term.

Texas / Dallas-Fort Worth. INSTRUMENT: state SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on qualifying data center equipment, not a property tax abatement (local sales tax is still due for the standard program). Tex. Tax Code Sec. 151.359: 10 years from certification for 200-249M USD capex, 15 years for 250M USD+ capex within 5 years, plus 20 qualifying jobs and 100,000 sq ft in a single building. Tex. Tax Code Sec. 151.3595 'qualifying large data center project': 20 years, 500M USD capex, 40 jobs, 20 MW contracted, 250,000 sq ft, and it exempts state AND local sales tax. Comptroller page last updated 20 Feb 2026. OBSERVED TERMS (the only observed US term data): the Comptroller's registry at https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/data-centers/data-center-lists.php was read for effective-to-end date spans. 5 facilities show full-term (non-revoked) spans: NADC 09/2013-09/2023 = 10 yr; LinkedIn Richardson 02/2014-02/2029 = 15 yr; State Farm Richardson 06/2015-06/2030 = 15 yr; Microsoft SAT09-SAT13 12/2015-12/2035 = 20 yr; Winner LLC 06/2015-06/2035 = 20 yr. Median = 15 years. Both DFW-market facilities in that set (LinkedIn Richardson, State Farm Richardson) are exactly 15 years, which is what this row records. Six further rows with end dates (Cedarvale, Cipher Black Pearl, Giga Texas, Hockley, Lonestar Taproot x2, TX11) show spans of 1 month to 4 years and were excluded as revocations/terminations, not scheduled expirations.

Arizona / Phoenix. INSTRUMENT: transaction privilege (sales) and use TAX EXEMPTION on qualifying equipment under the Computer Data Center program, A.R.S. Sec. 41-1519 - an equipment tax exemption, not a property tax abatement. NCSL 50-state survey (updated 1 Apr 2026) records the term as 10 or 20 years depending on sustainability certification, with a 2033 program sunset. Confirmed on the Arizona Commerce Authority program page (https://www.azcommerce.com/incentives/computer-data-center-program/): 'up to 10 full calendar years following certification', extended to 'up to 20 full calendar years' for Sustainable Redevelopment Projects; capex 50M USD within 5 years in Maricopa/Pima counties, 25M USD elsewhere; ACA may accept certification applications only between 1 Sep 2013 and 31 Dec 2033. Value records the standard 10-year term because Phoenix sits in Maricopa County and most projects certify under the standard tier.

Georgia / Atlanta. INSTRUMENT: state and local SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on data center equipment (high-technology data center exemption, O.C.G.A. Sec. 48-8-3(68.1)) - an equipment exemption, not a property tax abatement. Georgia Dept of Audits and Accounts tax incentive evaluation (Dec 2022) states 'Data centers must meet the investment threshold within seven years of their exemption start date', which is the operative term of a certificate; thresholds are tiered by county population (25M USD under 30,000; 75M USD for 30,000-50,000; 250M USD over 50,000 - Fulton/DeKalb/Douglas etc. in the Atlanta market fall in the 250M USD tier). SUNSET: sources conflict and this matters. The 2022 audit says the exemption sunsets in 2033 (as extended by HB 1291, 2022); Alston and Bird, 12 Feb 2026 (https://www.alston.com/en/insights/publications/2026/02/georgia-sales-tax-exemptions-data-centers) states it 'is set to expire on December 31, 2031'; NCSL (1 Apr 2026) says 2032. Treat the sunset as 2031-2033 and note that five 2026 bills (SB 408, SB 410, SB 436, HB 559, HB 1012) would repeal, suspend or pause it.

Ohio / Columbus. INSTRUMENT: SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on data center equipment under Ohio Rev. Code Sec. 122.175, granted by agreement with the Ohio Tax Credit Authority - not a property tax abatement. The statute sets no maximum: 'The term of an agreement under this section shall be determined by the tax credit authority'; eligibility is 100M USD capital investment plus 1.5M USD annual payroll at the site. In practice the awarded term is 15 years: Signal Ohio (30 Jul 2025) reports that for Microsoft's New Albany facility, in the Columbus market, 'the state Tax Credit Authority gave the company a 100% sales tax exemption for 15 years'. NCSL (1 Apr 2026) describes Ohio's as up to 15 years. IMPORTANT CURRENT STATUS: Governor DeWine announced on 27 May 2026 that he directed the Tax Credit Authority to pause consideration of any NEW data center tax exemption requests (https://governor.ohio.gov/media/news-and-media/governor-dewine-announces-pause-of-data-center-tax-exemption); existing agreements are unaffected, so 15 years remains the term of an agreement already in force.

Illinois / Chicago. INSTRUMENT: SALES TAX EXEMPTION certificate under the Illinois Data Centers Investment Program (20 ILCS 605/605-1025) covering state and local sales taxes on equipment, plus a construction-jobs income tax credit; there is also an optional local property tax abatement that a taxing district may grant separately. DCEO states the exemption is issued in '5-year increment certificates that are renewable' within a '20-year life span'; thresholds are 250M USD capex over 60 months and 20 new full-time jobs at 120% of county median wage, with a carbon-neutral or green-building certification required within 2 years. NCSL (1 Apr 2026) records 20 years with renewal every 5 years and no new certificates after 2029. CURRENT STATUS: the DCEO page states that per the Governor's directive DCEO 'will no longer process applications for the data center incentive program as of July 1, 2026', so the 20-year term applies to existing certificate holders, not to a new entrant.

Utah / Salt Lake City. NOT FOUND as a number, and this is a definitional gap rather than a research failure, so the value is left null rather than 0 (0 would wrongly read as 'no incentive available'). The Utah Code text effective 1 Jan 2026 was read directly: the qualifying data center / web search portal establishment exemptions (subsections at 59-12-104) carry no term of years, no expiration and no sunset - they are permanent statutory exemptions claimed by any taxpayer that meets the size test, with no agreement and therefore no agreement term. Utah Admin. Code R865-19S-122 (amended 13 Dec 2018) likewise sets no term. I found no data-center-specific PROPERTY TAX abatement in Utah; county-level property tax relief is discretionary and generic. So there is no 'typical term in years' to record. Cox's late-May 2026 executive order setting 'a Higher Bar for Data Center Development in Utah'.

Texas / Bexar (San Antonio). Same statutes and same instrument as the DFW row: state SALES AND USE TAX EXEMPTION on equipment, not a property tax abatement. Tex. Tax Code Sec. 151.359 gives 10 years at 200-249M USD capex and 15 years at 250M USD+; Sec. 151.3595 gives 20 years (state and local sales tax) for a qualifying large data center project at 500M USD capex, 40 jobs, 20 MW and 250,000 sq ft. Comptroller page last updated 20 Feb 2026. Market-specific caveat stated plainly: the only San Antonio facility in that set, Microsoft SAT09-SAT13 (12/15/2015 to 12/15/2035), runs 20 years because it is registered as a large data center project; San Antonio's other registered facilities (ALE60, ALE61, San Antonio Data Center II) are standard qualifying data centers with no end date posted yet. n = 5 facilities used statewide, 1 of them in the San Antonio market.

Oregon / Portland (Hillsboro, Washington County). Oregon has NO SALES TAX AT ALL, so 'no sales tax' is not an abatement and is not what this row measures. INSTRUMENT: local PROPERTY TAX ABATEMENT. Two instruments exist. (1) Enterprise zone: 100% property tax abatement on new qualified capital assets; the City of Hillsboro Q&A dated 8 May 2026 states 'Each application covers a period of 3 to 5 years. That is the maximum exemption period allowed.' Value 5 = the maximum standard enterprise-zone term, low 3 = the minimum. (2) Strategic Investment Program: a longer property tax abatement on assessed value above a taxable threshold for very large investments, documented at up to 15 years (https://www.stackinfra.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/Portland_Tax_Incentives_022421.pdf), which is the high bound; standalone data centers in Hillsboro are now negotiated through SIP. CURRENT STATUS: both are frozen. Oregon HB 4084 (passed March 2026) imposed a one-year statewide moratorium on new data center tax exemptions beginning 6 Jun 2026, and Hillsboro City Council approved a 180-day pause on new SIP agreements for standalone data centers on 21 Jul 2026 (https://hillsboronewstimes.com/2026/07/22/hillsboro-pauses-more-data-center-tax-breaks-to-close-potential-loophole/).

Nebraska / Omaha. Value is 0 because the data-center-specific instrument no longer exists. Neb. Rev. Stat. Sec. 77-2704.62, the data center sales and use tax exemption cited by NCSL's 1 Apr 2026 survey, now reads on the Nebraska Legislature's own statute page: 'Repealed. Laws 2026, LB901, Sec. 43.' operative 1 July 2026. The remaining route, the ImagiNE Nebraska Act (sales and use tax refunds, personal property tax exemptions, investment and wage credits), was closed to data centers by Governor Pillen's executive order signed 21 July 2026, which bars all new data center project applications from ImagiNE credits (https://nebraskaexaminer.com/2026/07/20/pillen-rescinds-imagine-act-tax-incentives-for-new-nebraska-data-centers/). What I checked: NCSL survey, Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2704.62, ImagiNE Nebraska Act materials, Good Jobs First coverage of the repeal. Existing agreements signed before these dates are unaffected, but a new Omaha project has no data-center-specific term to record.

Iowa / Des Moines. TWO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS, both sales and use tax exemptions, neither a property tax abatement. (1) Equipment: Iowa Code Sec. 423.3(95) exempts computers, equipment and related purchases for data centers meeting the investment threshold (200M USD for the full exemption; smaller partial-refund tiers at 1M and 10M USD) - this one is PERMANENT, with no term of years, tied to the investment threshold. (2) Electricity and fuel: H.F. 976, signed and effective 9 June 2025, put a clock on the energy exemption for the first time - indefinite for data centers already operating before 6 June 2025, 10 years for new or expanded facilities in cities with population over 30,000, and 15 years in cities of 30,000 or fewer. Des Moines has roughly 215,000 residents, so a new Des Moines-market facility gets the 10-year energy exemption, which is the value recorded; 15 is the rural high bound. NCSL (1 Apr 2026) corroborates '10-15 years beginning 2025' and notes the 30-new-job / 200M USD-in-6-years requirement and clawback if 80% of the investment threshold is missed.

Nevada / Reno (Storey and Washoe counties). TWO INSTRUMENTS RUNNING TOGETHER, which is unusual: a SALES AND USE TAX ABATEMENT (rate reduced to 2%) and a PERSONAL PROPERTY TAX ABATEMENT (75% of tax due), both under NRS 360.754 with the property piece at NRS 361.0683. Nevada GOED's data center fact sheet (Aug 2025) sets two tiers: 25M USD capital investment and 10 full-time Nevada-resident jobs gives 10 years of each abatement; 100M USD and 50 jobs gives 20 years of each. All requirements must be met within the first 5 years of operation and wages must be at least 100% of the statewide average. Value 20 records the tier that Reno-market hyperscale campuses (Tahoe Reno Industrial Center, Storey County) qualify for; 10 is the small-project floor. NCSL (1 Apr 2026) corroborates the 2% sales tax rate, the up-to-75% personal property abatement and the 50%-Nevada-resident construction labor condition.

Not applicable as a queue wait: Singapore does not operate a grid interconnection queue for new data centres, so there is no number of years to report. Since the 2019-2022 moratorium was lifted, new data centre capacity in Singapore is ALLOCATED, not queued - the Economic Development Board (EDB) and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) run a periodic Data Centre Call for Application (DC-CFA) in which operators bid and capacity is awarded competitively on published criteria (energy efficiency/PUE, green energy commitment, economic contribution, resilience), with EMA governing the underlying power system. Cited page is EDB's 1 December 2025 media release launching the second call (DC-CFA2): at least 200MW of capacity made available, with more possible via new green energy pathways; registration of interest closed 5 December 2025 and the application window closed 31 March 2026. The first round (DC-CFA1, 2023) awarded roughly 80MW in total to Equinix, GDS, Microsoft and an AirTrunk-ByteDance consortium. Consequence for the model: an operator without an award has no interconnection timeline at all, and an awardee's timeline is set by the award and build schedule rather than by a utility queue - so a numeric value here would be fabricated.
